newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX prods, crude get support from Tosco outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX prods, crude get support from Tosco outage.

text.p: NYMEX crude and oil product futures were firmer Thursday, helped by an outage at Tosco Corp's Bayway, New Jersey plant, futures traders said.

January crude, which ended sharply lower Wednesday after a bearish American Petroleum Institute report and resumed Iraqi crude exports, started 40 cents higher Thursday but had slipped back to $23.55 a barrel by just after 1100 EST, up just 17 cents on the day.
"It's completely news-driven off Tosco," said Al Lindseth, a trader at GSC Energy in Atlanta. "Without that news it was expected to go down some more."
"It's all Bayway. Once the story starts to fade to the background again the prices are going to fade," said Nauman Barakat, a trader Prudential Securities.

Sources close to Tosco reported on Thursday that there was a problem at its fluid catalytic cracking unit at Bayway on Wednesday night, which resulted in a small fire and the closure of the unit for an uspecified time.
The FCC there is among the largest and most sophisticated in the world, with a rated capacity of 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) out of a total plant processing capacity of 290,000 bpd.

"Given the inventory situation in the northeast, the fact there are 24 different types of gasoline there and that Bayway is the most sophisticated refinery in the world, it's been supportive," said Lindseth.
There was also some short-covering across the board after losses of more than $2 a barrel in the last few days on crude and similar amounts on the products.
But the direction of the market depends on how technical levels hold up this session and on Friday and on the outlook for the weather in the northeast after the current mild six-to-10-day outlook.
"We anticipate the market will have difficulty getting beyond $24.42, the 50 percent retracement of the decline from the highs," said analysts at Pegasus Econometrics in a daily report.
